text:
alex: Heads-up, after last week's eu-west burst we hit ENI limits in the westeurope cluster. Thinking we should roll out a Karpenter regional-affinity + soft-drain flow to avoid mass parallel launches. Any objections?

maria: +1. Can you paste the ENI attach error output so we know the failure mode?

alex: paste log: `Failed to attach ENI: eni-0abcd1234 exceeded ENIs per instance` — saw ~40 node creates in 10m, many in the same AZ.

sam: Was that from the cluster-autoscaler or Karpenter? If Karpenter then we probably had provisioning concurrency spikes. We can limit parallelism per provisioner.

jing: Karpenter supports topology constraints and instanceTypeFamilies. We should prefer family packing (e.g., instanceTypeFamilies: [g5, g4dn]) and tune `consolidation` to reduce fragmentation.

leo: Also propose a soft-drain pattern: annotate nodes `redwood.io/soft-drain=true` and run a daemonset that evicts non-critical pods over a tuning window so we don't trigger huge parallel node terminations/creates. We tried a variant in staging with good results.

carol: Note on spot fallback: if we do spot -> on-demand fallback aggressively we might double ENI churn because on-demand types differ. Need a cap on max nodes spawned per AZ and a fallback limit.

alex: Agreed. Draft proposal: 1) enable regional-affinity zone balancing in provisioner to spread launches across AZs, 2) implement soft-drain daemonset + 45s preemptive eviction window, 3) admission webhook to block hostNetwork/hostPort on low-capacity AZs, 4) cap concurrent launches per provisioner to 6.

maria: How do we implement soft-drain? Example manifest?

alex: Example snippet: 
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: soft-drain-helper
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: soft-drain-helper
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mover
        image: redwood/soft-drain:canary
        args: ["--evict-delay=45s", "--label=redwood.io/soft-drain"]
```
This daemonset watches nodes with the annotation and slowly cordons + evicts tolerant pods.

sam: Also add a node annotation `redwood.io/target-family=g5` so the scheduler prefers packing and avoids scattering across dozens of families.

jing: For testing: canary in eu-central first. Run a synthetic load that creates 60 concurrent GPU pods: 
```bash
kubectl create deployment gpu-load --image=busybox --replicas=60 -- /bin/sh -c 'sleep 10000'
kubectl patch deployment gpu-load -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"gpu-load","resources":{"requests":{"nvidia.com/gpu":"1"}}}]}}}}'
```
(leverage our test harness to throttle to AZs)

leo: We'll need telemetry: add metrics `provisioner_sync_duration`, `node_launch_rate`, `eni_attach_errors` and a grafana panel for ENI errors by AZ, plus an alert when ENI errors > 3/min per AZ.

carol: Cost/latency tradeoff: packing saves cost but increases cold-start tail latency when we start new nodes. Did we measure the impact?

alex: We ran an A/B in staging: packing + consolidation gave ~30% lower GPU spend but increased 95th token latency (cold) by ~8-15% for a small class of latency-sensitive jobs. For batch workloads it's fine; for interactive, maybe use an exemptions label.

maria: Proposed timeline?

alex: Canary schedule: Tue 03:00 UTC -> run 6h with synthetic and controlled customer-like traffic. Rollback triggers: ENI errors > 5/min, node crashloop > 2 nodes, or pod evictions > 10% for stateful workloads.

sam: I'll own canary validation and run chaos scripts to simulate AZ spike.

jing: I'll land the daemonset + admission webhook and the grafana dashboards.

leo: I'll update the infra runbook with rollback commands and the exact `kubectl` snippets to revert provisioner changes.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by alex at 1953456800 UTC — canary artifacts: notary://canary-19534568

alex: Thanks all — tagging follow-ups: @maria @sam @jing. I'll open a PR with the provisioner patch and the soft-drain daemonset after this thread.

carol: One more thing — can we add a temporary quota check in the control plane to reject large parallel requests if remaining ENI capacity < threshold? That avoids hitting AWS quota hard.

alex: Good idea. I'll prototype a lightweight pre-check in the provisioner shim that queries quota and returns `capacity-limited` when under threshold.

maria: Sounds good. See you on the canary. :thumbsup:
